title: Best AI Dictation App for Windows (2026)
summary: We ranked the best AI dictation apps for Windows in 2026, from Aqua Voice to Dragon, plus the free voice typing tools Windows already ships.
body_markdown:
For most people, Aqua Voice is the best AI dictation app for Windows in 2026: it runs natively on Windows 10 and 11, types into any app you use, and lets you fix your words by voice as you go. Windows also ships free voice typing (Win+H) that is worth trying first. Dragon, Superwhisper, and open-source Whisper tools fit narrower needs.


Windows dictation has a quiet problem the "best app" lists rarely admit. Most of the polished voice tools people rave about were built on a Mac first, and the Windows version arrived later, thinner, and slower to update. At the same time, Windows already includes two free voice features that a lot of searchers do not know exist. So before you pay for anything, it helps to know what you already have, and then which paid apps actually earned a place on a Windows PC.


## First: the free voice tools already on your PC


Windows 11 ships two separate voice features, and they are not the same thing. People conflate them constantly, so start here.


**Win+H (Voice typing).** Press the Windows key and H in any text field and a small voice bar appears. Speak, and it types. It is cloud-based, so it needs an internet connection, and it works on Windows 10 and 11. It handles everyday email and messages fine. It has no custom vocabulary, no way to edit by voice, and its accuracy drops on technical terms, names, and anything with unusual spelling.


**Voice Access.** This is the accessibility tool. It does dictation too, but its real job is full hands-free control of the PC: opening apps, clicking, scrolling, and moving windows by voice. It uses on-device recognition and works offline once set up, and it needs Windows 11 (22H2 or later). If you cannot use a keyboard and mouse at all, this is the built-in answer.


Our honest advice: try Win+H for a day. If it is fast and accurate enough for the writing you do, you may not need a paid app at all. Most people who go looking for a "best dictation app" do so because Win+H kept mangling the words that matter to them, which is exactly where a dedicated model earns its keep.


## What makes a dictation app good on Windows specifically


- **Accuracy on the words you actually use.** General speech models do well on plain prose and stumble on names, jargon, product names, and code. That is where the gap between tools shows up.
- **A real Windows build, not a port.** Check whether the app treats Windows as a first-class platform or as a Mac app that got a late Windows sibling. Version parity and update cadence tell you a lot.
- **System-wide dictation.** The best tools type into every app: Word, Outlook, Chrome, Slack, the terminal, a CRM field. Anything locked to one window is a step backward from Win+H, which already works everywhere.
- **Editable text.** Dictation still misfires. Being able to correct a word by voice, without reaching for the keyboard, is the difference between a demo and a daily tool.
- **Honest pricing.** Watch the gap between the annual and monthly numbers, and whether one subscription covers your other devices.


## The best AI dictation apps for Windows in 2026


### 1. Aqua Voice: best overall for accuracy and everyday use


[Aqua Voice](https://aquavoice.com/) runs natively on[Windows 10 and 11](https://aquavoice.com/windows) , types into any app, and is built around a simple idea: your first draft should be close enough that you rarely touch the keyboard. It is powered by Avalon, Aqua's own dictation model, which was the #1 proprietary model on the OpenASR leaderboard at its October 2025 debut. On Aqua's self-reported AISpeak benchmark it scores 97.3% accuracy, and in a 9to5Mac head-to-head on the same passage it made 1 error where the built-in dictation made 17.


Two things set it apart on Windows. First, a custom dictionary and a model tuned for real vocabulary, so names, technical terms, and product names come out right instead of phonetically. Second, Voice Edit Mode: you can speak a correction ("change that to quarterly") and Aqua rewrites the text, rather than forcing you to retype. Final text lands in around 450ms and you can dictate at up to 230 WPM.


Pricing is the other reason it tops the list. Every account starts with 1,000 free words for life, no card required. Pro is $8/mo billed annually for unlimited dictation, and one subscription covers Windows, Mac, and iPhone, which matters if you move between machines. See the[guide](https://aquavoice.com/guide) for setup and voice commands.


**Best for:** anyone who wants the most accurate everyday dictation on Windows without paying enterprise prices, especially people who write a lot of names, jargon, or code.


### 2. Wispr Flow: the polished cross-platform pick


Wispr Flow is the best-known name in this category, and it genuinely runs on Windows, Mac, iOS, and Android. It is fast, clean, and pleasant to use. If your priority is one familiar tool across every device including Android (which Aqua does not support), it is the obvious choice.


The tradeoff is cost. At the time of writing, Wispr Flow's paid tier runs roughly $12 to $15 per month, which is meaningfully above Aqua's $8/mo billed annually for a similar core job. If you want the head-to-head detail, we keep an[Aqua vs Wispr Flow](https://aquavoice.com/vs/wispr-flow) comparison up to date.


**Best for:** people who need Android coverage or want the most mainstream, polished option and do not mind paying more.


### 3. Dragon Professional v16: the specialized Windows powerhouse


Dragon is the veteran, and on Windows it is still a serious tool. Dragon Professional v16 is Windows-only (there has been no Mac version since 2018), and it is sold as a one-time perpetual license for roughly $700 at the time of writing, with no subscription. What you get for that is deep custom command macros, industry vocabularies, and the kind of hands-free control that regulated fields like law and medicine have relied on for years.


For most people in 2026 that is more tool, and more money, than the job needs, and the experience feels dated next to the newer AI models. But if you dictate all day into specialized workflows and need programmable voice commands, Dragon is still the pick. We wrote a fuller take in our[Dragon alternatives](https://aquavoice.com/blog/dragon-alternatives-for-mac) piece (Mac-focused, but the honest split between dictation and hands-free control applies to Windows too).


**Best for:** high-volume professionals in medicine, law, or accessibility who need custom commands and can justify the price.


### 4. Superwhisper: the offline, private option


Superwhisper is built for people who want their audio to stay on their machine. It runs local speech models (you can choose local Whisper builds) so nothing has to leave the device, which is a real requirement for some users. Its accuracy and offline story are strong.


The Windows caveat is important and it is vendor-verifiable: Superwhisper started on the Mac, and at the time of writing its Windows build trails the more mature Mac version in features and polish. If you are on Windows specifically, check the current Windows release notes before committing.


**Best for:** privacy-first users who need fully offline dictation and can accept a younger Windows app.


### 5. Open-source Whisper apps: free and fully local


If you are comfortable with a little setup, a wave of free, open-source Windows dictation tools now wrap OpenAI's Whisper (which they disclose openly) to run entirely on your PC. Projects like OpenWhispr and GigaWhisper offer push-to-talk dictation with no cloud, no subscription, and no telemetry. You trade convenience and polish for total control and a $0 price tag.


**Best for:** tinkerers and privacy purists who want local dictation for free and do not mind configuring it.


## How to set up dictation on Windows with Aqua Voice


1. Go to[aquavoice.com/windows](https://aquavoice.com/windows) and download the Windows app (Windows 10 or 11).
2. Sign in. Your account starts with 1,000 free words, no card required.
3. Grant microphone access when Windows prompts you.
4. Set your push-to-talk key, then hold it, speak, and release. The text appears wherever your cursor is, in any app.
5. To fix something, hold the key and say the correction. Voice Edit Mode rewrites the text instead of making you retype.


That is the whole loop. Because it works system-wide, the same flow covers Word, Outlook, Chrome, Slack, your terminal, and any form field.


## FAQ


**Does Windows already have built-in dictation?** Yes. Press Win+H in any text field for voice typing (cloud-based, Windows 10 and 11), or use Voice Access for hands-free PC control (on-device, Windows 11). Both are free. A dedicated app like Aqua Voice adds higher accuracy on names and jargon, a custom dictionary, and the ability to edit text by voice.


**What is the most accurate dictation app for Windows?** Accuracy depends on your vocabulary, but Aqua Voice leads on the words that trip up general models. It runs on Avalon, the #1 proprietary model on the OpenASR leaderboard at its October 2025 debut, and reports 97.3% accuracy on its own AISpeak benchmark.


**Is there a free AI dictation app for Windows?** Yes. Windows' built-in Win+H voice typing is free, Aqua Voice gives you 1,000 free words with no card, and open-source tools like OpenWhispr run locally for free if you are willing to set them up.


**Do I need Dragon for Windows in 2026?** Only for specialized, high-volume work that depends on custom voice command macros and industry vocabularies. For everyday dictation, a modern AI app like Aqua Voice is more accurate out of the box and far cheaper than Dragon's roughly $700 license.
